subject: Transportation Systems
title: Immersed Tube Tunnels
description: A fast breakdown of Immersed Tube Tunnels for builders.

hook.text: Some tunnels aren't dug—they're floated into place. Prefabricated sections sink into a trench on the seabed.

buildup.text: Each section is built in a dry dock, sealed, towed to position, and sunk into a pre-dredged channel.

discovery.text: Once positioned, sections are connected underwater and the joints sealed. Water is pumped out to finish.

twist.text: Immersed tubes work best in shallow water with soft seabeds. Deep rock makes this method impossible.

climax.text: Hong Kong's Cross-Harbour Tunnel and the San Francisco BART tube both used this technique.

punchline.text: Sometimes building a tunnel means sinking it, not digging it.

quiz.question: How are immersed tube tunnels constructed?
options: Prefabricated sections are floated and sunk into a pre-dug seabed trench
